launch-fl-tampa-curtis-hixon-waterfront-.summary: Tampa's central riverfront lawn and event park, linking seasonal splash fountains, a shaded playground, separate dog areas, water-taxi access, museums, Kiley Garden and the Tampa Riverwalk.
launch-fl-tampa-curtis-hixon-waterfront-.hours: Park grounds are open daily from 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. The Louvre splash fountain normally runs April-October from 9:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. and November-March from 10:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m.; water features can stop for cold weather, maintenance or events.
launch-fl-tampa-curtis-hixon-waterfront-.parking: The William F. Poe Garage at 800 North Ashley Drive is the most practical general option, with metered street spaces and other downtown garages nearby. Event days can fill the closest facilities and change rates.
launch-fl-tampa-curtis-hixon-waterfront-.arrival: Use Ashley Drive for the lawn, playground and museums. The park is also directly on the Tampa Riverwalk, with a boat dock and Pirate Water Taxi stop along the river edge.
launch-fl-tampa-curtis-hixon-waterfront-.restrooms: Public restrooms are shown near the central park facilities, but museum and nearby business restrooms follow their own admission and hours. Confirm availability during large events or late visits.
launch-fl-tampa-curtis-hixon-waterfront-.cost: The park, playground, splash fountains, dog areas and Riverwalk are free. Parking, water taxi rides, museums, food and ticketed events cost separately.
launch-fl-tampa-curtis-hixon-waterfront-.accessibility: The main lawn edges, Riverwalk, playground approach and museum connections are paved and broadly level. Use Poe Garage accessible parking or the nearest legal drop-off for the shortest route.
launch-fl-tampa-curtis-hixon-waterfront-.dogs: Dogs are welcome on leash outside the designated dog areas. Separate small- and large-dog parks opened in 2026; dogs remain excluded from playground and splash-water areas under posted rules.
launch-fl-tampa-curtis-hixon-waterfront-.family: The shaded playground and seasonal fountains sit close together, with museums immediately beside the park. Bring water and sun protection because the Great Lawn is exposed despite shaded seating near play areas.
launch-fl-tampa-curtis-hixon-waterfront-.transit: TECO Line Streetcar, HART buses, Downtown Tampa DASH, Pirate Water Taxi and Riverwalk routes all serve the downtown waterfront; verify the closest current stop for your approach.
launch-fl-tampa-curtis-hixon-waterfront-.need: The Great Lawn is a major event venue, so concerts and festivals can fence sections, limit ordinary access and change parking. Check the City event calendar and fountain status before a water-play trip.

launch-fl-tampa-lettuce-lake-park.summary: A popular Hillsborough River conservation park with a long swamp boardwalk, wildlife viewing, a paved exercise loop, nature center, native garden, picnic shelters and two inclusive playgrounds.
launch-fl-tampa-lettuce-lake-park.hours: Open daily from 8:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. in spring and summer and 8:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m. in fall and winter. Gates and individual facilities may close earlier for weather or construction.
launch-fl-tampa-lettuce-lake-park.parking: Pay the $2 vehicle entry fee at the entrance and use the lot nearest your destination. Lot E is the practical current approach to the east boardwalk entrance while the nature-center-side entrance is renovated.
launch-fl-tampa-lettuce-lake-park.arrival: For the current open boardwalk approach, follow park signs toward Parking Lot E. The entrance behind the Joel E. Jackson Nature Center is closed during renovation.
launch-fl-tampa-lettuce-lake-park.restrooms: Restrooms are available in the developed picnic and visitor areas. Do not count on a facility once you are deep on the boardwalk or loop; use one before starting the route.
launch-fl-tampa-lettuce-lake-park.cost: Entry is $2 per vehicle for up to eight people, cash only according to the current county page. Shelter rentals and programs cost separately; canoe and kayak rentals are currently suspended.
launch-fl-tampa-lettuce-lake-park.accessibility: The paved 1.25-mile loop, new adaptive playground equipment and developed areas provide accessible options. Construction currently affects the boardwalk entrance and observation tower, so follow the posted accessible route.
launch-fl-tampa-lettuce-lake-park.dogs: Leashed pets are allowed in ordinary park areas but are not permitted on the boardwalk. Bicycles are also prohibited on the boardwalk.
launch-fl-tampa-lettuce-lake-park.family: Two playgrounds added in 2024 include swings, adaptive and sensory equipment and a nature scavenger hunt. The shaded boardwalk is a strong wildlife outing, but supervise children closely by water and railings.
launch-fl-tampa-lettuce-lake-park.transit: HART service runs along the Fletcher Avenue corridor, but the park entrance and internal destinations can require a substantial walk. A car or rideshare is generally the simplest approach.
launch-fl-tampa-lettuce-lake-park.need: As of June 2026, sections of the boardwalk are under repair, shelters 5 and 7 and the observation tower are closed, and the canoe/kayak launch and rentals are suspended. Enter the boardwalk from the east side near Lot E.

launch-fl-tampa-julian-b-lane-riverfront.summary: A 25-acre west-bank riverfront park with a fenced play cove, large splash pad, sports courts and field, dog park, lawns, public art, rowing boathouse, boat access and skyline views.
launch-fl-tampa-julian-b-lane-riverfront.hours: Outdoor park areas generally follow posted City park hours. The splash pad normally runs April-October from 9:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m. and November-March from 10:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m.; event spaces and organized athletics keep separate schedules.
launch-fl-tampa-julian-b-lane-riverfront.parking: Use the onsite lots and legal spaces reached from North Boulevard, choosing the north end for dog and boat access or central/south areas for play and athletics. Festivals and tournaments can sharply reduce availability.
launch-fl-tampa-julian-b-lane-riverfront.arrival: The park is long rather than compact. Choose the Play Cove and splash pad, River Center, dog park and docks, Festival Lawn or sports courts before arriving instead of navigating only to the general pin.
launch-fl-tampa-julian-b-lane-riverfront.restrooms: Restrooms are available in developed park facilities, with the most dependable access near the main activity and event areas. Building access can vary around private events.
launch-fl-tampa-julian-b-lane-riverfront.cost: General park, playground, splash pad, courts, lawns, public art and dog park are free. Reservations, programs, food, water taxi service and special events may charge.
launch-fl-tampa-julian-b-lane-riverfront.accessibility: Paved routes connect major facilities, and the park is a City pilot location for Lazarillo inclusive digital navigation for blind visitors. Confirm the closest parking for the feature you need.
launch-fl-tampa-julian-b-lane-riverfront.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in ordinary outdoor areas. Separate large- and small-dog sections are at the north end; dogs should stay out of play and splash areas.
launch-fl-tampa-julian-b-lane-riverfront.family: The fenced play cove serves ages 2-12 and combines shaded equipment and seating with a large splash bucket nearby. Pack dry clothes and confirm water operation on cool or stormy days.
launch-fl-tampa-julian-b-lane-riverfront.transit: HART routes serve North Boulevard and downtown connections, while Riverwalk routes and water taxi stops reach the river edge. Check event detours before relying on the closest stop.
launch-fl-tampa-julian-b-lane-riverfront.need: There is little reason to cross the whole 25 acres if you choose the right arrival point. Summer heat and lightning affect exposed lawns and water access, and special events can reserve or fence major spaces.

launch-fl-tampa-ballast-point-park.summary: A South Tampa bayfront park with sunrise views, a playground, seasonal splash pad, picnic shelters, gazebo, boat ramp and dock, fitness center and seafood concession.
launch-fl-tampa-ballast-point-park.hours: The park is open daily from 6:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. The current featured-park page lists splash-pad hours as 8:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m.; the citywide seasonal schedule may vary, so confirm before a water-play visit.
launch-fl-tampa-ballast-point-park.parking: Free park parking is available but limited and busiest around weekends, sunrise and family activity times. Only four trailer spaces serve the single-lane boat ramp and they fill quickly.
launch-fl-tampa-ballast-point-park.arrival: Use Interbay Boulevard for the main playground, splash pad, shelters and waterfront. Boat-ramp users should continue to the designated ramp area and avoid ordinary car spaces with a trailer.
launch-fl-tampa-ballast-point-park.restrooms: Restroom access is associated with the developed park and fitness/concession area. Hours can be shorter than the 24-hour boat ramp, so plan accordingly for early or late launches.
launch-fl-tampa-ballast-point-park.cost: General park, playground, splash pad, views and ordinary picnic use are free. Food, fitness memberships, reservations, rentals and required fishing licenses cost separately.
launch-fl-tampa-ballast-point-park.accessibility: Developed park areas have paved connections and nearby parking, but hurricane repair zones can change the waterfront route. Use the closest signed accessible space and obey barriers.
launch-fl-tampa-ballast-point-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in ordinary park areas, subject to posted exclusions around the playground, splash pad and food service. There is no dedicated off-leash area.
launch-fl-tampa-ballast-point-park.family: A semi-shaded playground with a tot area sits near the flower-style splash pad, benches and picnic shelters. The bayfront has open edges and active boat traffic, so maintain close supervision.
launch-fl-tampa-ballast-point-park.transit: HART bus service reaches the Interbay and Bayshore area, but frequency and the final walk should be checked before relying on transit. Cycling from Bayshore Boulevard is another option.
launch-fl-tampa-ballast-point-park.need: The 600-foot fishing pier remains closed because of major damage from Hurricanes Helene and Milton; do not plan a pier walk or fishing trip there. The boat ramp remains open 24 hours, separate from park hours.

launch-fl-st-petersburg-vinoy-park.address: 701 Bayshore Drive Northeast, St. Petersburg, FL 33701
launch-fl-st-petersburg-vinoy-park.summary: A broad downtown bayfront lawn and waterfront trail known for skyline views, walking, running, cycling, festivals and easy connections to North Shore parks and the Pier district.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-vinoy-park.hours: The park opens 30 minutes before sunrise and closes at 11:00 p.m. Event fencing and improvement work can limit portions independently.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-vinoy-park.parking: Use legal metered street spaces or downtown garages and lots; the park does not offer enough dedicated parking for major-event demand. Expect road closures and event pricing during festivals and races.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-vinoy-park.arrival: Bayshore Drive Northeast and Fifth Avenue Northeast meet at the park. Choose the south end for downtown and Pier connections or the north end for North Shore and palm-arboretum connections.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-vinoy-park.restrooms: Do not assume an unlocked restroom is available in every part of the open lawn. Nearby staffed waterfront facilities and businesses have separate hours and access rules.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-vinoy-park.cost: Ordinary park and trail access are free. Parking, food, rentals and ticketed festivals or concerts cost separately.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-vinoy-park.accessibility: The waterfront recreation trail and primary lawn edges are paved and broadly level, though temporary event surfaces, fencing and improvement work can alter routes.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-vinoy-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in ordinary outdoor areas. Events may impose additional restrictions, and owners should keep dogs away from crowded athletics or food areas.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-vinoy-park.family: The open lawn and paved waterfront route work well for strolling and views, but this is not primarily a playground park. Pair it with the St. Pete Pier or North Shore facilities for child-focused play.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-vinoy-park.transit: The free Downtown Looper and local transit serve the downtown waterfront, with bike and pedestrian links along the bay. Event road closures may relocate stops.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-vinoy-park.need: A large park improvement project is currently closing part of Vinoy Park. This is also a major event venue, so check City notices before expecting an uninterrupted lawn or ordinary parking.

launch-fl-st-petersburg-st-pete-pier.summary: A free 26-acre waterfront district extending into Tampa Bay with a large playground, splash pad, small beach, fishing deck, discovery center, public art, lawns, market, tram and multiple food options.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-st-pete-pier.hours: The Pier opens 30 minutes before sunrise and closes at 11:00 p.m. Glazer Family Playground runs 7:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. and the Majeed Foundation Splash Pad 9:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m.; businesses keep separate hours.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-st-pete-pier.parking: More than 500 paid onsite spaces are available in the Dolphin and Pelican lots and along Pier Drive, but parking is limited to six hours. Peak demand is typically Friday 4:00-9:00 p.m. and Saturday 1:00-8:00 p.m.; downtown garages are useful for longer visits.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-st-pete-pier.arrival: Enter from Second Avenue Northeast. Families may stop near the playground and splash pad, while the free accessible tram reduces the roughly half-mile trip to Pier Point.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-st-pete-pier.restrooms: Public restrooms are available at multiple developed Pier locations, including family-oriented areas. Use the posted Pier map because the district is much longer than it appears from the entrance.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-st-pete-pier.cost: Pier entry, playground, splash pad, Spa Beach, lawns and public art are free. Parking, food, discovery-center admission, retail and some events cost separately.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-st-pete-pier.accessibility: The main promenade is paved, an accessible tram carries wheelchairs, and developed attractions include step-free routes. Wheelchairs and strollers are not rented onsite.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-st-pete-pier.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed in ordinary outdoor Pier areas but not on Spa Beach or in the Majeed Foundation Splash Pad. Businesses may set separate pet rules.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-st-pete-pier.family: The playground, splash pad, beach, Discovery Center and food options can fill several hours. Bring sun protection and dry clothes; water-play supervision and beach conditions remain the caregiver's responsibility.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-st-pete-pier.transit: The free Downtown Looper stops at the Pier entrance about every 15 minutes, and the Central Avenue Trolley, SunRunner connections, bicycles and pedestrian routes serve downtown.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-st-pete-pier.need: Onsite parking has strict time limits and no overnight parking. Check current art and attraction notices before visiting; Bending Arc is presently listed as temporarily closed, and lightning can stop water activities.

launch-fl-tierra-verde-fort-de-soto-park.address: 3500 Pinellas Bayway South, Tierra Verde, FL 33715
launch-fl-tierra-verde-fort-de-soto-park.summary: A 1,136-acre Gulf park across five keys with nearly three miles of beach, a historic fort, dog beach, fishing piers, campground, boat ramp, playgrounds and a seven-mile paved trail.
launch-fl-tierra-verde-fort-de-soto-park.hours: Open daily from 7:00 a.m. to sunset. Campground, boat-ramp, museum, concession and pier operations have separate schedules, and severe weather can close exposed areas.
launch-fl-tierra-verde-fort-de-soto-park.parking: A $6 daily vehicle parking fee applies and is paid by app, pay-by-text or onsite terminals; mobile payment adds a $0.35 convenience fee. Pay stations are distributed near the beaches, piers, dog park, fort and headquarters.
launch-fl-tierra-verde-fort-de-soto-park.arrival: The park is enormous and driving between destinations takes time. Navigate specifically to North Beach, East Beach, Historic Fort, dog beach, a fishing pier, campground or boat ramp rather than the general park pin.
launch-fl-tierra-verde-fort-de-soto-park.restrooms: Restrooms and outdoor rinse showers are distributed near major beaches, picnic areas, campground and developed facilities. Remote trail and shoreline stretches have fewer services.
launch-fl-tierra-verde-fort-de-soto-park.cost: The daily parking fee is $6 per vehicle. Camping, boat launching, concessions, rentals and reservations cost separately; ordinary beach, fort and trail access do not add a general admission fee.
launch-fl-tierra-verde-fort-de-soto-park.accessibility: A 2,200-foot Barrier-Free Nature Trail, accessible facilities and beach-access features serve visitors with mobility needs. Sand, tides and storm damage can still alter practical access.
launch-fl-tierra-verde-fort-de-soto-park.dogs: Dogs are allowed on the designated dog beach and in separate fenced large- and small-dog areas with water stations. Outside designated areas, leash and exclusion rules apply; dogs are not allowed on ordinary swimming beaches.
launch-fl-tierra-verde-fort-de-soto-park.family: North Beach, playgrounds, shallow-water areas, fort exploration and picnic shelters support a full family day. Conditions can change rapidly, so check flags, tides, heat and storms and bring substantial water and sun protection.
launch-fl-tierra-verde-fort-de-soto-park.transit: There is no practical frequent transit for most visitors. Driving, cycling for experienced riders or a prearranged ride are the usual options; verify return transportation before being dropped off.
launch-fl-tierra-verde-fort-de-soto-park.need: A burn ban has been in effect since February 2026, and construction or maintenance can affect facilities. Check rip-current, lightning, red-tide/water-quality, nesting-wildlife and County closure notices on the day of the trip.

launch-fl-st-petersburg-boyd-hill-nature.address: 1101 Country Club Way South, St. Petersburg, FL 33705
launch-fl-st-petersburg-boyd-hill-nature.summary: A 400-acre urban nature preserve beside Lake Maggiore with trails through multiple Florida habitats, wildlife viewing, a raptor aviary, education programs, pioneer settlement and campground.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-boyd-hill-nature.hours: March-October: closed Monday; Tuesday-Friday and Sunday 9:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m., Saturday 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m., with trails closing at 6:30 p.m. November-February hours end at 6:00 p.m., with trails closing at 5:30 p.m.; holiday closures apply.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-boyd-hill-nature.parking: Free onsite parking is available near the environmental education center entrance. Arrive early for cool-weather weekends and scheduled programs, when the closest spaces can fill.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-boyd-hill-nature.arrival: Enter from Country Club Way South and check in at the Lake Maggiore Environmental Education Center before using preserve trails. Trail access closes before the front gate hours.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-boyd-hill-nature.restrooms: Restrooms are available near the education-center and developed entrance area during operating hours. Use them before longer loops; interior trail facilities are limited.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-boyd-hill-nature.cost: Daily admission is $3 per adult, $1.50 for children ages 3-16 and free under age 3. Annual passes, camps, tours and special programs have separate pricing.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-boyd-hill-nature.accessibility: The entrance facilities and some routes support mobility access, while natural trails include sand, roots, uneven surfaces and exposed sections. Ask staff for the most suitable current route.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-boyd-hill-nature.dogs: Pets are not appropriate on preserve trails because of protected wildlife; follow posted preserve restrictions. Qualified service animals are handled under applicable access rules.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-boyd-hill-nature.family: The raptor aviary, habitat trails and programs create a strong wildlife-learning visit. Bring water, insect repellent and sun protection, and never approach or feed alligators or other wildlife.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-boyd-hill-nature.transit: Local bus service reaches the Lakewood area, but the final approach and limited schedule should be checked carefully. A car or rideshare is typically simpler.
launch-fl-st-petersburg-boyd-hill-nature.need: The nature center's exhibits are currently closed for renovation, although the preserve and trails remain open. Mondays are closed, trail entry ends before facility closing, and heat or lightning can shorten a safe visit.
